scenario.description: A district director of operations must approve the conversion of one of two unused classrooms into a small culinary teaching lab, including the room, equipment configuration, seating capacity, and procurement method, with input from the principal, the culinary teacher, and the purchasing coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The high school has requested approval to convert either Room 204 or Room 206 into a culinary teaching lab.
shared_context.S2: The draft request proposes 16 student seats, two cooking ranges, and a completed installation before the next academic term.
shared_context.S3: Both rooms are currently unused and have passed the district's initial general facilities inspection.
shared_context.S4: Ms. Okafor makes the binding facilities and procurement decision.
shared_context.S5: At the weekly facilities approval meeting, Ms. Okafor asks the principal, culinary teacher, and purchasing coordinator for relevant operational details before finalizing the request.

PF1.text: Room 204 is the high school's designated severe-weather shelter and must retain enough clear floor area for 30 people. Room 206 is the approved alternative for the lab, but its usable floor area limits the culinary lab to exactly 12 student seats. Mr. Bennett confirmed both points against the current emergency plan and facilities records this week, but the conversion request used an outdated room inventory.

PF2.text: Room 206's existing circuit supports exactly four portable induction burners, and four burners are sufficient for the planned student rotations. Ms. Liu tested the circuit and revised the lesson rotations this week, but the equipment count in the request remains two commercial ranges.

PF3.text: The awarded facilities grant permits purchases only through a grant purchase order, limits each equipment item to $2,500, and excludes built-in gas installations. Mr. Rios reviewed the grant amendment after it arrived yesterday, but the request packet has not yet been updated.

acceptance_conditions: The lab must be assigned to Room 206 so Room 204 remains available as the severe-weather shelter.
The equipment plan must use exactly four portable induction burners.
The plan must exclude any built-in gas installation.
The project must use a grant purchase order.
The student seating capacity must be reduced to exactly 12.
Each equipment item must be capped at $2,500.
A facilities-and-shelter commitment must be recorded.
An electrical-load commitment must be recorded.
A grant-compliance commitment must be recorded.
The emergency-plan fact must be cited after being stated aloud.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['facilities_and_shelter', 'room_selection', 'document_update', 'packet_update', 'request_packet_update'] for c in commitments) or any('shelter' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['electrical_load', 'equipment_specification', 'equipment_list_revision', 'instructional_plan_confirmation'] for c in commitments) or any('circuit' in c['detail'] or 'electrical' in c['detail'] or 'induction' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] in ['grant_compliance', 'procurement_compliance', 'request_packet_update', 'packet_update'] for c in commitments) or any('grant' in c['detail'] or '$2,500' in c['detail'] or '2,500' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The emergency-plan restriction changes the room from the proposed choice of Room 204 to Room 206, and the facilities record changes seating from 16 to exactly 12 while requiring a shelter-related commitment and citation.
The tested circuit and revised lesson rotations change the equipment plan from two commercial ranges to exactly four portable induction burners and require an electrical-load commitment.
The grant amendment changes procurement to a grant purchase order, excludes built-in gas installation, sets the exact $2,500 per-item cap, and requires a grant-compliance commitment.
